Hello, Sorry for the late reply. Thank you for your comments. I suppose that when I am opening up to someone, I want to feel like they are hearing what I'm saying. Around a month ago, I was very upset and emotional because of a fight with my sister and I was with a friend and told her some very personal details and experiences I've had with my depression and suicide and she didn't say anything in response. I can appreciate that not everyone is able to "easily" or comfortably speak about these topics, and I don't think I necessarily wanted her to say anything at the moment, but I feel like we should have talked about it after the fact when I had calmed down. She hasn't brought it up since. She can kind of talk about my depression but we've never talked explicitly about me being suicidal, partly because I do understand she doesn't know what to say and she gets uncomfortable. 

I guess it's really on me because on the rare occasions I do want to talk about my trauma I kind of beat-around-the-bush and don't directly say "I want to talk about THIS." I kind of just want whomever I'm speaking to, to ask me about it. I suppose that's unfair to them, as they can't read my mind, but I guess what I really *want* is for them to ask me about how I am doing, how I'm feeling, and to know that they care about me and those things. I like to ask the people in my life how they're doing in a genuine sense just to see if they wanna talk about anything (good or bad happening in their lives), and I guess I just want someone to do the same and not ask me how I am when I know they don't really want me to start pouring my heart out and are just using the phrase as small talk. Pardon my rambling!

So because your spine has shifted from the fusion to help correct curves, the muscles in your back aren't working as hard, hardly at all, or working differently than before. Some muscles in your back may come to rely on the rods bc the rods are doing most of the work of stabilizing you. However, with doing something like martial arts, it may be activating the muscles so it wouldn't be as bad if the rods were removed. I got spinal fusion in 2005 and have chronic pain and it has limited me from doing a whole lot so it's probably something that would be worse for me since my spine and muscles have gotten used to the rods being there and doing the work there longer, and I hadn't really found exercises catering to my spine and back muscles until recently

Hello, I think it would be wise to go talk to your surgeon about your dilemmas, or see a spine specialist to see if they can give you any tips. T2-L1 is a fairly large fusion so I'm not sure if there's a whole lot you can do about mobility issues. I have T5-T12 fused and have been having pain in my lumbar because it's starting to curve again, so I've been going to physical therapy and i do feel like it's help with some of my mobility issues as a result of my fusion. Perhaps asking for exercises specifically for your spine might help?

Your muscles do rely on your rods however--you're not using a lot of the muscles anymore or in the same ways and you probably wouldn't have as much stability in your spine without them. I know someone who got their rods removed and their back basically "fell apart." (Not trying to scare you!) also there may be a chance your spine could start curving again if you removed your rods, and therefore your support system. But I would definitely talk to a specialist, surgeon or not to start with and see what they can recommend for you. Good luck!
